spec_round_protocol.why: Operator: 'one agent produces the spec, the next triggers the agents review until a agent thinks is good to implement. We need to have another gate so agent don't go on forever.' Implemented as successive driver iterations rather than subagents, at the operator's suggestion ('the trigger at 2AM generates the spec and the one at 2:15 reviews it'). A fresh process has no memory of writing the thing it reviews, so the independence is structural rather than merely prompted.
spec_round_protocol.gate: At round 3 without approval, STOP iterating. Ship the artifact as-is, record every unresolved objection in decisions_for_user, and move to the next queue item. Never a fourth round.
how: AUTHOR iteration: write or revise the artifact. Set next_action to 'REVIEW <path> round <K>'. Commit.

REVIEW iteration: read the artifact cold. Do NOT look up who wrote it. Critique against the item's stated review_criteria. Then either (a) set approved=true in the log and set next_action to the implementation step, or (b) write concrete objections and set next_action to 'REVISE <path> round <K+1>'. Commit.
Record the round number in the log entry every time, so the gate is auditable.
spec_round_protocol.research: Web research is authorised and encouraged where it would change the answer. Operator: 'Do any research on the internet that the agents deem necessary. Always think things out before implementing.'

queue.title: Fix the conversation-inheritance tie properly, with a sequence column
queue.why: hub/tests/test_override_inheritance.py::test_the_most_recent_overrides_win fails ~50% in a full chunked run. The test is CORRECT; the code is wrong. A trustworthy suite is a precondition for Q5's audit — a loop culling tests cannot tell a flake from a test it broke.
queue.detail: DO NOT apply the one-line fix proposed in handoff 0050 (adding Conversation.id.desc()). Prep checked it and it does not work: Conversation.id is 'conv-' + short_id(), i.e. random, so id.desc() picks the later-created row only about half the time. It would make the query deterministic-looking while staying arbitrary. The real bug: hub/hub/conversations.py:72 orders by created_at.desc() alone, and two conversations created inside the same clock tick tie — on Windows the default timer granularity is ~15.6ms, so this hits real users, not just tests. Follow the codebase's own precedent: add an autoincrement `sequence` integer primary key to Conversation, exactly as TaskTransition and InboundQueueEntry already do, and read the reasoning already written at hub/hub/db/models.py:695-699. Order by sequence.desc(). Needs a migration in hub/hub/migrations/versions/ that guards for a missing table (see 0033/0034), and CLAUDE.md requires bumping the head assertions in BOTH hub/tests/test_migrations.py and hub/tests/test_project_persistence.py.
queue.verify: Add a regression test that creates two conversations with an identical created_at and asserts the later one wins. Mutation-check it: revert the ordering change and watch that named test fail. Then run the full hub suite three times and confirm test_override_inheritance passes every time.

NEW, found and fixed while building Q4-spec-ux-fixes phase 6 (F5's drawer), worth knowing generally rather than just in that commit: a naive 'click outside this panel closes it' listener (checking only `panelRef.current.contains(event.target)`) breaks against any Radix-portaled control opened from inside that panel — Radix's `DropdownMenu`/`Select`/etc. portal their open content to a sibling of `document.body`, outside the panel's own DOM subtree, so a click on a menu item reads as a board click and closes the panel out from under the menu mid-selection. Fixed in TaskDetailDrawer.tsx by also excluding clicks inside `[data-radix-popper-content-wrapper]`. Caught by a mutation-checked regression test, not anticipated in the design doc — worth checking if any other future click-outside-to-close surface in this codebase reuses raw containment checks near a Radix trigger.
